literacy.angry: Anger usually turns up when something seems unfair, or when we wanted something badly and could not have it. It arrives fast, and takes longer to leave than it took to come.
literacy.sad: Sadness usually turns up when we lose something we liked, or when things did not go the way we hoped. It settles in slowly and stays a while. With someone beside you it does not pass any faster — but it is easier to carry.
literacy.scared: Fear turns up to tell us to be careful. It does not mean the thing is dangerous, and it does not mean you have to stay put. Fear gets smaller when we come closer slowly — not when we run away.
